claim: For ungapped, unambiguous aligned DNA sequence pairs of common length \(L\), let \(t\) and \(v\) be the numbers of transition and transversion differences, respectively, let p-distance be \(p=(t+v)/L\), and let the Kimura two-parameter distance be \(K=-\frac12\log(1-(2t+v)/L)-\frac14\log(1-2v/L)\), restricted to its finite real domain \(2t+v<L\) and \(2v<L\). No two admissible count signatures receive opposite strict distance rankings from \(p\) and \(K\) for \(L\le8\). Weak-order agreement first fails at \(L=3\): one transition and one transversion both have p-distance \(1/3\) but different K2P distances. At \(L=9\), strict reversal appears for the first time, and there is exactly one unordered reversing pair of count signatures: \((t,v)=(2,3)\) versus \((4,0)\). Their p-distances are \(5/9>4/9\), whereas their Kimura distances satisfy \(\frac14\log(243/4)<\log 3\). Equivalently, against the common reference `AAAAAAAAA`, the sequences `GGCCCAAAA` and `GGGGAAAAA` are ordered in opposite ways: p-distance selects the latter as nearer, while K2P selects the former. The proof is exhaustive because K2P comparison is equivalent to reverse ordering of the exact integer \(F_L(t,v)=(L-2t-v)^2(L-2v)\), and every admissible transition/transversion signature is realizable relative to a common reference.
integrity: K2P ordering is reduced exactly to reverse ordering of the positive integer \(F_L(t,v)=(L-2t-v)^2(L-2v)\). The packaged verifier exhausts every admissible integer signature and every pair through \(L=9\), and independently checks an explicit common-reference sequence realization.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns ungapped, unambiguous equal-length DNA comparisons on the finite real domain of the standard K2P formula. The unique nine-site witness is highly divergent and near the correction boundary; the result is a sharp finite mathematical boundary, not a frequency claim for ordinary low-divergence barcodes.
title: Nine sites are the sharp p-distance–Kimura nearest-neighbor reversal boundary
